title: The Coaching Habit: Say Less, Ask More & Change the Way You Lead Forever
author: Michael Bungay Stanier
target_audience: Business professionals aiming to develop coaching skills
Anyone interested in improving workplace communication and development
core_themes: The power of asking questions over giving advice
Creating habit change for better leadership
Encouraging growth and learning in teams
primary_purpose: To teach leaders and managers how to adopt a simple, practical approach to everyday coaching that helps make coaching a regular, informal part of their daily leadership practice—focusing on asking more questions and offering less advice.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, practical, and concise with a focus on actionable advice
structure_format.organization: Organized into chapters based on the seven essential coaching questions, with supporting insights and tactics to integrate coaching habits

key_concepts_lessons: Coaching can be quick and informal and integrated into any leadership role.
Asking questions is more powerful than offering solutions.
Seven essential questions form the backbone of effective coaching (e.g., The Kickstart Question, The AWE Question, The Focus Question, etc.).
Building habits is key to consistent coaching behavior.
Active listening and curiosity are central to developing others.
Leaders should resist the urge to immediately give advice.
Empowering employees to find their own solutions leads to greater engagement and growth.
notable_features: Focus on seven core questions for everyday coaching
Habit-formation science and techniques for sustaining new behaviors
Backed by research but designed for immediate application
Appealing design with humor and illustrations
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2010s, the book reflects a growing move in business towards empowering people through coaching rather than directive management style. As organizations became flatter and more collaborative, coaching skills were seen as essential for modern leaders.
reception_impact: Bestseller in leadership and business categories worldwide
Praised for its brevity, clarity, and actionable tactics
Widely adopted in corporate leadership training programs
Credited with making coaching skills accessible to non-professional coaches
Some readers seek deeper exploration beyond the foundational tactics
comparable_titles: Co-Active Coaching by Henry Kimsey-House, Karen Kimsey-House, et al.
Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us by Daniel H. Pink
